target_customer: Software companies with usage-based or multi-tenant cloud and AI infrastructure costs that need per-customer and per-feature cost attribution
problem: Cloud and LLM bills are opaque, so software companies cannot tell which customers or features are profitable or price correctly.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for cloud cost analytics

founders.name: Micah Wheat
founders.background_notes: Strategy and sales background per the YC page.

founders.name: Adam Shugar
founders.background_notes: Engineering background per the YC page. The two met at Stanford.

technical_complexity.rationale: Attributing costs per endpoint invocation and customer requires instrumentation, observability data and joining cloud billing, which is standard engineering with some hard parts for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Several FinOps vendors offered per-customer cost views and the approach could be copied. Integration into a customer's telemetry gave modest lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. Rhombus, a physical security company that was its own customer, acquired it in February 2025.

market_need_then: Cloud spend and the rise of LLM API costs in early 2023 made unit economics per customer a growing concern for SaaS companies.

branding.domain_note: Used dashdive.com; the company was formerly named Rosettic, per CB Insights and YC URL history.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found no press, community or brand material about Dashdive's identity, so no brand pull is shown.

outcome_analysis: Dashdive stayed a two person company that raised only a small amount per aggregators and was acquired by Rhombus in February 2025. Rhombus already used the product to track cloud costs per camera and customer, so the deal looks like a customer buying a tool it depended on rather than a venture scale exit. Terms were not disclosed.
notes: The dashdive.com website redirects to rhombus.com, so the site is now the acquirer's. CB Insights reports about $500K raised over 3 rounds with Rhombus, Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator as investors, but no per-round breakdown, so no round is recorded and the figure is unverified. Deal date is 2025-02-27 per PitchBook and a 2025-03-03 news listing per CB Insights. No dated competitor sources near the 2023 batch were found. success_factors uses other because no taxonomy code fits a customer acquisition.
